The Compass Beside the White Stone

白色石头旁的指南针 · 648 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A hiking group set off into a mountainous region. A campsite lay beyond a grassy valley near a snowy peak. A map showed a pine forest stretching around a lake, a rocky cliff, and a hollow basin. Ada, the guide, had checked the weather. Mist covered a white stone as they approached the first bend. A child could not see the leading hiker. Ada stopped the group before anyone tried to descend the steep slope.

2The compass pointed east. A folded map made the route look straight. A boy wanted to creep forward for a glimpse of the horizon. Ada saw a narrow ditch in the mud and boot marks close to a sheer drop. The old trail used to cross that fringe. A newer path curved around the cliff. Hazy light made its first turn hard to distinguish. She unfolded the whole map instead of judging the direction from one small strip.

3Ada unfolded the map atop a flat boulder. A chalk dot marked the place they had passed. She could follow the next stretch by its shape rather than by a distant view. The climb led around a stony ridge and then downward through woods. A boy asked how long the detour would take. She estimated forty minutes if the ground stayed dry. A patch of dew made the next stone slippery, so she allowed more time. A slower descent would still bring them to the campsite before dark.

4A chilly wind blew through the valley. The pupils stopped behind a wall and opened a pack. One had brought a ski map by mistake. One pulled on a jumper. Another read the temperature aloud in degrees Celsius. Ada checked the altitude. A deep hole should be visible at that elevation. She saw it beneath tall grass and marked it with a pencil. A second leader proposed a route across the basin. Ada asked him to keep to the wooded incline while the faraway slope was still misty.

5They followed the curve toward a cave. Geologically the soft chalk was unusual in that hilly district. A pupil found an irregular piece near a boot mark. Ada asked him to compare the rock with the one drawn on the map. The path past it offered a useful second sign. An eagle appeared briefly above the fringe of the forest. She waited until they had two firm landmarks rather than make a decision based on a shape in a gloomy sky.

6Running water crossed the next path. A pole showed its depth. The leader looked for a place to leap over it, but Ada did not want the younger pupils to dare each other. They found a wooden bridge and followed a gentle upward trail. The sky was still overcast when they reached a hut. A strip of sunshine broke through and let them see the cliff again. The group could now tell where an apparently straight route would have become perilous.

7At the hut an older guide asked whether the group had come to enjoy the scenery or conquer the peak. The children had planned to explore the wilderness. They could postpone the summit without losing that chance. One had slipped on wet dirt and wanted to retreat. The guide showed them a lower loop by a stream. It was still windy outside, but the loop offered a safe return if they left after a break.

8A child asked what would happen if the party wandered past the first bend. Ada showed him the compass and a stone from the old trail. Natural landmarks were tricky to read when mist moved downwards across the cliff. He drew the ditch, the two posts, and a pit beside the bridge. Then he told a waiting group where to stop. The route sounded safer once he could describe its first turn rather than point at the far extremity of the valley.

四级汇总词汇 · 34中文译文

白色石头旁的指南针

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一队徒步者出发进入山区。积雪的山峰附近有一道长满草的山谷，营地就在山谷另一边。地图画出了环湖的松林、岩石峭壁和一片凹下去的盆地。向导阿达已经看过天气。队伍快到第一个转弯时，雾遮住了旁边一块白石头。一个孩子看不见走在最前的人。阿达叫大家停下，免得有人贸然下陡坡。

2指南针指向东边。地图折起来后，那段路线看着像一条直线。一个男孩想悄悄走上前，看看远处的天际。阿达看到泥里有一道窄沟，靴印已经很靠近陡崖边缘。老路从那片边缘穿过，新路则绕开峭壁。雾气让第一个转弯很难辨认。她把地图全摊开，仔细看整段路线。

3阿达把地图摊在一块平坦的大石上，用粉笔点出刚走过的地方。即使看不见远处，她也可以根据形状辨认下一段。路线先爬坡，绕过石头多的山脊，再穿林向下。一个男孩问绕路要多久。她估计，如果地面一直干燥，要四十分钟。前面有块石头沾了露水，很滑，她就多留了一点时间。慢慢下山，仍能在天黑前到营地。

4山谷里刮来一阵寒风。孩子们在一道墙后停下，打开背包。有人带错了滑雪地图，有人套上了套头衫，还有人念出了摄氏温度。阿达核对海拔。按这个高度，附近应该看得见一个深坑。她在高草下找到了坑，用铅笔做了记号。另一位领队提议横穿盆地。远处的斜坡还在雾里，阿达请他先沿着有树林的坡走。

5他们沿弯道向一个洞穴走去。从地质上说，这片丘陵很少见到这么软的白垩。有个孩子在靴印旁捡到一块形状不规则的石头。阿达请他拿地图上画的那块来比。经过那块石头的小路给了他们第二个辨认方向的标志。一只鹰短暂飞过林缘。阿达等到确认两个可靠的地标才作决定，因为阴沉天空中的轮廓很容易看错。

6下一条路有流水横过。一根竿子显示了水深。领队想找地方跳过去，阿达怕小孩子互相起哄，也去试跳。大家找到一座木桥，沿着缓坡往上走。到达小屋时，天仍然阴着。一线阳光透下来，大家重新看见了峭壁。现在他们终于看清，原先看似笔直的路线会在哪一段变得危险。

7小屋里，一位资深向导问，大家是来看风景的，还是来登顶的。孩子们原本就想探索野外，登顶推迟了也不妨碍这件事。一个孩子在湿土上滑过一跤，想返回。向导给他们看了溪边地势更低的一条环路。外面还是有风，休息后走那条路就能安全回去。

8一个孩子问，队伍要是走过了第一个弯怎么办。阿达给他看指南针，也让他看老路上的一块石头。雾顺着峭壁往下压时，自然地标不容易认。孩子画出了沟、两根柱子和桥旁的坑，然后告诉另一支等着出发的队伍在哪里停。等他能把第一个弯说清楚，只要听他描述的人，就知道该从哪里绕开危险。
